content.value_statement: Teams lose time fixing vague or inconsistent commit history. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft Sentry-style conventional commits with clear issue references.
actual_capabilities: Formats commit headers with type, optional scope, and subject.
Applies Sentry commit types such as feat, fix, ref, docs, and test.
Adds issue footers using Fixes or Refs patterns.
Suggests branch naming that matches the commit type.
Provides examples for fixes, features, refactors, breaking changes, and reverts.
limitations: It does not inspect repository changes unless the agent is separately asked to do so.
It cannot verify that issue IDs exist in GitHub, Sentry, or Linear.
It does not create commits by itself.
It focuses on Sentry conventions, which may differ from other projects.

use_cases.title: Prepare a clear commit
use_cases.description: Draft a conventional commit message that explains a small code change and links the right issue.

use_cases.title: Standardize pull request history
use_cases.description: Rewrite local commit messages so reviewers see consistent types, scopes, and subjects.

use_cases.title: Document release-impacting work
use_cases.description: Create commit text for breaking changes, fixes, or refactors that must be easy to audit later.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Sentry-style commit message for this change: [describe the change]. Include a suitable type and concise subject.

prompt_templates.title: Add an issue footer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry commit message for [change]. Use scope [scope] and reference issue [issue ID] without closing it.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing message
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this commit message to follow Sentry conventions: [paste message]. Keep the meaning and make each line under 100 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a breaking change
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Sentry-style breaking change commit for [change]. Include motivation, migration impact, and the correct footer format.

output_examples.input: A deleted user can return null and crash the dashboard. Issue SENTRY-5678 should close on merge.
output_examples.output:
fix(api): Handle null response in user endpoint

Add a null check before reading deleted account properties. This prevents dashboard crashes for removed users.

Fixes SENTRY-5678

output_examples.input: Alert updates should reply in the original Slack thread. Link GH-1234 without closing it.
output_examples.output:
feat(alerts): Add Slack thread replies for alert updates

Post updates and resolutions to the original Slack thread so related notifications stay grouped.

Refs GH-1234

output_examples.input: A previous feature commit must be reverted because it caused production performance issues.
output_examples.output:
revert: feat(api): Add new endpoint

This reverts the previous endpoint change.

Reason: Caused performance regression in production.

best_practices: Describe the actual code change before asking for a commit message.
Provide the issue ID and whether the commit should close or only reference it.
Review the final message for repository-specific scopes and release impact.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a message without explaining what changed and why.
Do not use Fixes when the commit should not close the issue.
Do not combine unrelated changes into one commit message.

faq.question: Does this skill create git commits?
faq.answer: No. It helps write commit messages and branch guidance. The user or agent must run git commands separately.

faq.question: What commit style does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Sentry conventions based on conventional commits, with types, optional scopes, body text, and issue footers.

faq.question: Can it write breaking change commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for exclamation-mark headers and BREAKING CHANGE footers.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub and Linear references?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include GH numbers, hash issue references, Sentry issue IDs, and Linear-style Refs footers.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it during development?
faq.answer: Yes. It is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when drafting commit messages for code changes.

faq.question: Does it check whether the branch is correct?
faq.answer: No. It provides branch naming guidance, but branch checks require separate git commands and user approval.
